beats.say: A jar buried in Egypt held over seven and a half kilos of Indian pepper.
beats.cap: 7.5+ kg of Indian pepper, buried in Egypt

beats.say: Its value? About two years of wheat for one Roman.
beats.cap: Worth ≈ 2 years of a Roman's wheat

beats.say: This was Berenike, a Red Sea port of Roman Egypt.
beats.cap: Berenike: Red Sea port, Roman Egypt

beats.say: Monsoon winds carried ships here from India's Malabar coast.
Why so far south? To dodge the northern Red Sea's strong winds.
beats.cap: Why so far south? Northern winds

beats.say: Caravans carried it across the desert to the Nile, then Rome.
Indians lived here too, for a while.
A jar shard reads "Korran the chieftain", in Tamil-Brahmi letters.
So Rome's hunger for pepper brought Indian traders to Egypt's coast.
